english.title: Breach a slavery and trafficking risk or prevention order
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without reasonable excuse, did something that you were prohibited from doing, namely **(..SPECIFY PROHIBITED ACT..), by

(A)_[a slavery and trafficking prevention order]_
(B)_[an interim slavery and trafficking prevention order]_
(C)_[a slavery and trafficking risk order]_
(D)_[an interim slavery and trafficking risk order]_
(E)_[a slavery and trafficking prevention order under Schedule 3 to the Human Trafficking and Exploitation (Criminal Justice and Support for Victims) Act (Northern Ireland) 2015]_
(F)_[an interim slavery and trafficking prevention order under Schedule 3 to the Human Trafficking and Exploitation (Criminal Justice and Support for Victims) Act (Northern Ireland) 2015]_

made by **(..SPECIFY COURT..) on **(..SPECIFY DATE OF ORDER..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 30(1) and 30(3) of the Modern Slavery Act 2015.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
without reasonable excuse
did something prohibited by an order mentioned in section 30(1)

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: An order of conditional discharge is not available to the court by or before which the defendant is convicted

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment

An order of conditional discharge is not available to the court by or before which the defendant is convicted

Time Limit for Prosecution:
None

Note
The maximum penalty on summary conviction may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates' court, see section 30(3)(b) of the Modern Slavery Act 2015. and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
